newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO sees global wheat trade volume at 10-year low.
newsitem.headline: FAO sees global wheat trade volume at 10-year low.

text.p: The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Monday that international trade in wheat in 1996/97 was expected to be at its lowest level by volume in a decade.

"Global wheat imports in 1996/97 (July/June) are currently forecast at 87.4 million tonnes, nearly eight million tonnes below the previous year but 3.4 million tonnes higher than anticipated in February," the Rome-based agency said.
FAO said in its latest food outlook that "despite this month's upward adjustment, international wheat trade would be the smallest in volume since 1986/87."
It said most of the decline would be in developing countries, where imports are expected to fall to 69.5 million tonnes, some seven million tonnes or nine percent below the previous year's level.
"The bulk of this year's contraction in international wheat trade would reflect smaller imports into Africa and Asia," the agency said.
